questions.s: A machine that cost Rs 120,000 has accumulated depreciation of Rs 45,000. It is sold for Rs 70,000 in cash. What is the result of the sale?
questions.e: Book value = 120,000 − 45,000 = 75,000. Sold for 70,000, so there is a loss of Rs 5,000. Comparing the price with cost alone ignores the depreciation already charged.

questions.s: A machine bought for Rs 200,000 is depreciated at 10 % a year on cost by the straight-line method. After exactly three years it is sold for Rs 150,000. What is the result of the sale?
questions.e: Depreciation = 20,000 a year, 60,000 over three years, so book value = 140,000. Sold for 150,000: profit of Rs 10,000. Rs 50,000 loss compares the price with the original cost.

questions.s: Which fixed asset is normally not depreciated?
questions.e: Freehold land does not wear out or expire, so it is usually not depreciated. Buildings, vehicles and computers lose value through use, time and obsolescence.

questions.s: An asset costs Rs 600,000, has a residual value of Rs 60,000 and a useful life of 9 years. By the straight-line method, what is the yearly depreciation as a percentage of cost?
questions.e: Yearly depreciation = (600,000 − 60,000) ÷ 9 = 60,000, and 60,000 ÷ 600,000 = 10 % of cost. 1 ÷ 9 ≈ 11 % ignores the residual value.

questions.s: When depreciation is accumulated in a separate provision account, which entry records the year's depreciation?
o: Provision for Depreciation Dr, Depreciation Cr
Depreciation Dr, Provision for Depreciation Cr
Asset Dr, Provision for Depreciation Cr
questions.e: Under this method the asset stays at cost; the year's charge is debited to Depreciation (closed to profit and loss) and credited to Provision for Depreciation, which is deducted from cost in the balance sheet.

questions.s: Which law governs partnership firms in Pakistan?
questions.e: Partnerships in Pakistan are governed by the Partnership Act, 1932. The Companies Act deals with companies, and the Negotiable Instruments Act with bills, notes and cheques.

questions.s: If the partners have no agreement on how to share profits, how are profits shared under the Partnership Act?
o: In the ratio of their capitals
In the ratio of time each spends on the business
In the ratio of their drawings
questions.e: Without an agreement, the Act says profits and losses are shared equally, whatever the capitals. Many students wrongly assume the capital ratio applies.

questions.s: If there is no partnership agreement, what interest is allowed on partners' capitals?
questions.e: In the absence of an agreement, partners get no interest on capital. The 6 % a year rule applies to loans a partner makes to the firm, not to capital.

questions.s: A partner lends money to the firm, and there is no agreement about interest. At what rate is interest allowed on the loan?
questions.e: Under the Partnership Act, a partner's loan to the firm earns interest at 6 % a year when nothing else is agreed. Capital, by contrast, earns no interest without an agreement.

questions.s: What is a partnership deed?
o: A certificate of incorporation from the government
A list of the firm's assets and liabilities
A written agreement setting out the partners' rights and duties
A bank document allowing partners to borrow
questions.e: The deed records matters such as capital, profit-sharing ratio, interest, salaries and drawings. A certificate of incorporation belongs to a company, not a partnership.

questions.s: Amir and Bushra share profits in the ratio 3 : 2. The firm's profit for the year is Rs 150,000. What is Bushra's share?
questions.e: Bushra's share = 2/5 × 150,000 = Rs 60,000; Amir gets Rs 90,000. Rs 100,000 wrongly uses 2/3 instead of 2/5.

questions.s: Faisal and Ghazala have capitals of Rs 400,000 and Rs 300,000. The deed allows 10 % interest on capital and a salary of Rs 24,000 a year to Ghazala, with the rest of the profit shared equally. Profit for the year is Rs 200,000. What is Faisal's total share?
questions.e: Interest: Faisal 40,000, Ghazala 30,000; salary 24,000; remaining 200,000 − 94,000 = 106,000, shared 53,000 each. Faisal = 40,000 + 53,000 = Rs 93,000. Rs 107,000 is Ghazala's total.

questions.s: How is interest charged on partners' drawings treated in the profit and loss appropriation account?
o: Debited, as an expense of the firm
Not shown; it goes to the balance sheet
Credited, as it adds to the profit to be shared
questions.e: Interest on drawings is charged to the partners (debit their current or capital accounts) and credited to the appropriation account, increasing the amount left to share.

questions.s: Under the fixed capital method, where are partners' interest on capital, salaries and drawings recorded?
questions.e: With fixed capitals, the capital accounts keep the original amounts and all regular items, such as interest, salary, share of profit and drawings, go through the current accounts.

questions.s: A partner withdraws Rs 60,000 on 1 July. Interest on drawings is charged at 10 % a year, and the year ends on 31 December. How much interest is charged?
questions.e: The money is out of the business for six months (July to December): 60,000 × 10 % × 6/12 = Rs 3,000. Rs 6,000 charges a full year's interest.

questions.s: What is the liability of a partner in an ordinary partnership firm?
o: Limited to the capital he has invested
Limited to his share of the profits
Nil, as only the firm is liable
questions.e: Partners have unlimited liability: if the firm cannot pay its debts, creditors may claim from a partner's private property. Limited liability is a feature of companies.

questions.s: Who draws a bill of exchange?
o: The debtor, who is to make payment
The bank that collects the bill
The creditor, who is to receive payment
questions.e: The drawer is the creditor who writes the bill ordering the debtor to pay. The debtor, who must pay, is the drawee.

questions.s: Who accepts a bill of exchange?
questions.e: The drawee, the debtor, signs the bill to show he agrees to pay on the due date. Once accepted, the drawee is called the acceptor.

questions.s: How many days of grace are added to a time bill of exchange in Pakistan when finding its due date?
questions.e: The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 adds three days of grace to the date on which a time bill falls due. Bills payable on demand get no days of grace.

questions.s: A bill of exchange dated 10 March is payable two months after date. What is its due date?
questions.e: Two months after 10 March is 10 May; adding three days of grace gives 13 May. 10 May forgets the days of grace.

questions.s: Tahir accepts a bill drawn on him by Usman for Rs 50,000. Which entry does Usman make?
questions.e: For Usman, the drawer, the accepted bill is an asset (Bills Receivable, debit) that replaces Tahir's debt (credit Tahir). Bills Payable appears in the drawee's books.

questions.s: Tahir accepts a bill drawn on him by Usman for Rs 50,000. Which entry does Tahir make?
questions.e: For Tahir, the drawee, his debt to Usman is replaced by a liability on the bill: Usman is debited and Bills Payable credited.

questions.s: Kashif holds a bill of Rs 40,000 accepted by Laila. On the due date it is dishonoured, and Kashif pays noting charges of Rs 500 in cash. Which entry does Kashif make?
o: Laila Dr 40,500; Bills Receivable Cr 40,000; Cash Cr 500
Bad Debts Dr 40,500; Bills Receivable Cr 40,500
questions.e: The bill is cancelled (credit Bills Receivable) and Laila again owes the amount plus the noting charges, which she must bear (debit Laila 40,500); the charges were paid in cash. Dishonour alone does not make the debt bad.

questions.s: Who makes a promissory note?
o: The debtor, who promises to pay
The payee, who will receive payment
questions.e: A promissory note is a written promise by the debtor (the maker) to pay. A bill of exchange, by contrast, is an order drawn by the creditor.

questions.s: Interest of Rs 1,500 credited by the bank appears only in the bank statement. Before the cash book is updated, how does its balance compare with the bank statement?
questions.e: The bank has added the interest but the business has not yet recorded it, so the cash book shows Rs 1,500 less. The bank column is then debited to update it.

questions.s: The bank statement shows a credit balance of Rs 62,000. Cheques issued but not presented total Rs 9,000, and cheques deposited but not yet credited total Rs 4,500. What is the cash book balance?
questions.e: Working back from the bank figure: deduct unpresented cheques (the cash book has already paid them) and add uncleared deposits (already in the cash book): 62,000 − 9,000 + 4,500 = Rs 57,500.

questions.s: The money received from selling an old machine is credited to the Sales account. What type of error is this?
questions.e: A capital receipt from selling a fixed asset has been treated as revenue from selling goods, which breaks an accounting principle. The trial balance still agrees.

questions.s: The credit total of a trial balance exceeds the debit total by Rs 900. How is the suspense account opened?
o: With a debit balance of Rs 900
With a credit balance of Rs 900
With a debit balance of Rs 450
With a credit balance of Rs 1,800
questions.e: Suspense goes on the shorter side. Debits are short by Rs 900, so the suspense account starts with a debit balance of Rs 900.

questions.s: The purchases book is overcast by Rs 2,000, and a suspense account has been opened. Which entry corrects the error?
questions.e: Overcasting means the Purchases account was debited Rs 2,000 too much, while suppliers were posted correctly. Credit Purchases to reduce it and debit Suspense.

questions.s: Under which method of depreciation does the book value of an asset never reach zero?
questions.e: A fixed percentage of a falling balance always leaves something behind, so the book value never reaches nil. Straight-line, also called fixed instalment, can write the asset down to zero.

questions.s: Furniture costing Rs 50,000 is depreciated at 20 % a year by the reducing balance method. What is its book value after two years?
questions.e: Year 1: 50,000 − 10,000 = 40,000. Year 2: 40,000 − 8,000 = Rs 32,000. Rs 30,000 deducts 10,000 in both years, as straight-line would.

questions.s: Partners share profits in the ratio 2 : 1. Profit for the year is Rs 90,000. What is the larger share?
questions.e: The larger share = 2/3 × 90,000 = Rs 60,000; the smaller is Rs 30,000. Rs 45,000 would be an equal split.

questions.s: If there is no partnership agreement, is a partner who works full-time in the firm entitled to a salary?
o: Only if profit is above a set level
questions.e: Under the Partnership Act, a partner gets no salary unless the partners have agreed one, however much work he does.

questions.s: On 1 April a partner lends Rs 200,000 to the firm. There is no agreement about interest, and the year ends on 31 December. How much interest is due to him for the year?
questions.e: With no agreement, a partner's loan earns 6 % a year. For April to December (9 months): 200,000 × 6 % × 9/12 = Rs 9,000. Saying no interest is due confuses a loan with capital.

questions.s: A bill of exchange dated 5 June is payable three months after date. What is its due date?
questions.e: Three months after 5 June is 5 September; adding three days of grace gives 8 September.

questions.s: A bill of Rs 60,000 is discounted with a bank two months before it is due, at 15 % a year. How much does the bank pay?
questions.e: Discount = 60,000 × 15 % × 2/12 = 1,500, so the bank pays Rs 58,500. Rs 51,000 charges a full year's discount.

questions.s: The cash book shows an overdraft of Rs 20,000. Cheques issued but not presented are Rs 5,000, and cheques deposited but not yet credited are Rs 8,000. What overdraft does the bank statement show?
questions.e: The bank has not yet paid the Rs 5,000 of cheques, so its overdraft is smaller by that much; it has not yet credited Rs 8,000 of deposits, so its overdraft is larger by that much: 20,000 − 5,000 + 8,000 = Rs 23,000.

questions.s: Repairs to machinery of Rs 5,000 were debited to the Machinery account. Before correction, how is the net profit affected?
questions.e: An expense has been treated as an asset, so expenses are Rs 5,000 too low and profit Rs 5,000 too high. The correction is Repairs Dr, Machinery Cr Rs 5,000.

questions.s: A bill dated 15 January 2025 is payable 60 days after date. What is its due date?
questions.e: Count 60 days after 15 January: 16 days left in January + 28 in February (2025 is not a leap year) + 16 in March = 60, giving 16 March. Adding three days of grace gives 19 March.

questions.s: A bill of Rs 100,000 with three months to run is discounted with a bank at 12 % a year. How much does the holder receive from the bank?
questions.e: Discount = 100,000 × 12 % × 3/12 = 3,000, so the bank pays Rs 97,000. Rs 88,000 charges a full year's discount.
